elements.evidence: The rendered clause still binds Customer (IBM): "Neither party will, for a period of twelve (12) months ... in any way solicit for employment any of the other party's personnel directly involved in performing this Agreement". Making the covenant mutual extends, rather than removes, a restriction on Customer, so the preferred 'no non-solicit on Customer' outcome is not achieved.

Operative sentence now opens "Neither party will ... solicit for employment any of the other party's personnel ... without the prior written consent of the other party", replacing the IBM-only obligation running to MSL.

elements.element: The restriction covers only personnel directly involved in the Services.
elements.evidence: Scope is limited to "the other party's personnel directly involved in performing this Agreement", replacing the former blanket coverage of "any Transferred Employees" irrespective of involvement.

elements.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months after the person's involvement ends.
elements.evidence: "for a period of twelve (12) months after the end of an individual's involvement in performing this Agreement" — duration and temporal anchor both match the checklist; the former "[*] years from the Effective Date" anchor is gone. Deterministic check 'non-solicit duration ≤ 12 months' ok=true.

elements.element: General advertisements are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: The retained carve-out reads "will not restrict or prevent IBM from ... b) by using general employment advertising or communications or independent search firms, hiring any person who responds thereto, provided that IBM does not direct or encourage such independent search firms to solicit such Transferred Employees." Two defects: (i) the carve-out's own proviso is conditioned on "such Transferred Employees", a term that no longer has any antecedent in the amended sentence (the restriction now speaks of "personnel directly involved in performing this Agreement"), so the exclusion turns on an undefined trigger; and (ii) the exception is drafted to excuse only IBM while the obligation it qualifies is now bilateral, leaving the mutual restriction without a general-advertising carve-out on the MSL side. Deterministic check 'general-solicitation carve-out present' ok=false is consistent with this substantive defect.

elements.element: Unsolicited approaches are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: "the foregoing will not restrict or prevent IBM from a) employing any such person who contacts IBM on his or her own initiative without any solicitation or encouragement from IBM" — the unsolicited-approach exclusion survives and operates for Customer; it depends on no undefined term ("such person" refers back to the other party's directly involved personnel).

elements.element: The restriction does not prohibit hiring.
elements.evidence: The covenant is limited to "solicit for employment"; no "employ or engage" or no-hire language appears, and the provisos expressly permit "employing any such person" and "hiring any person who responds thereto".

reasons: Fallback is incomplete: the general-advertising carve-out element fails. Repair in operative language by (i) replacing "such Transferred Employees" in limb (b) with "such personnel" (or "the other party's personnel directly involved in performing this Agreement") so the proviso has a live antecedent, and (ii) rewriting the chapeau of the proviso from "will not restrict or prevent IBM from" to "will not restrict or prevent either party from" (with "IBM" changed to "that party" in limbs (a) and (b)) so the carve-outs match the now-mutual restriction.

Preserves intent fails for the same reason: the amendment deletes "Transferred Employees" from the operative restriction but leaves the trailing reference "such Transferred Employees" dangling, and leaves a one-directional exception qualifying a bilateral obligation — an internally inconsistent retained sentence.
Preferred is not available on this draft as rendered: the redline retains (and extends to MSL) a non-solicit binding Customer rather than deleting Section 9.0(f)'s restriction on Customer.

Minimality is satisfied: the edit touches only the single restriction sentence needed for mutuality, involvement-based scope and the 12-month/involvement-end anchor, retains the existing carve-outs and the solicitation-only formulation, and adds no survival tail, expense language or extra procedure.
